A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeBridge and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The 24-page v3 and 26-page v4 support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v3 reports original long-term, short-term, and financial forecasting experiments, architectural ablations, and attention-map analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original forecasting and ablation results and adds a comparison of TimeBridge trained with hybrid MAE versus MSE loss.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same four-component pipeline and Equations 1–10, including moving-average detrending and both attention mechanisms. The proposed hybrid MAE objective also remains. Revised configurations and the MSE-loss ablation do not introduce a new component into the proposed method.

E1.justification: v4 removes Climate, representing precipitation across 1,763 Australian stations, from the evaluation and dataset appendix. The other long-term datasets, four PeMS datasets, and two financial datasets remain. The new loss ablation uses retained datasets.

E2.justification: Leddam replaces FEDformer in the long-term comparisons in Tables 1 and 9. DUET replaces FEDformer in the PeMS comparison in Table 2. The remaining comparator sets, including financial baselines, are retained.

E3.justification: The implementation appendix changes the reported training duration from 10 to 100 epochs. Table 8 revises several ETT and Traffic configurations, including attention-layer counts, patch counts, dimensions, learning rates, and loss weights. v4 also evaluates an MSE-loss control. These are substantial reported setting changes, although the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 15 tests whether TimeBridge's performance depends on hybrid MAE rather than MSE training, across eight retained datasets and with DeformableTST as a reference. Existing normalization, component-order, CI/CD, downsampling, and visualization analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Financial uncertainty reporting narrows: v3 Table 17 reports standard deviations for all six financial metrics, whereas v4 Table 18 retains only ARR, AVol, and MDD, dropping ASR, CR, and IR. The three-repeat statement and other statistical reporting practices remain.

E6.justification: v4 adds Leddam, DUET, and MSE-loss results and removes Climate results. DUET's added PeMS03 RMSE is 22.99, below TimeBridge's retained 23.10. Table 9 changes the ETTm1/336 PatchTST MAE from 0.392 to 0.369 and Crossformer MSE from 0.408 to 0.389. Retained TimeBridge main scores are numerically unchanged; the revised settings do not establish a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: v3 provides integration, cointegration, and ADF/EG background. v4 retains this and adds Appendix B with two propositions, a Brownian-motion-based attention-score derivation, and a differencing argument about losing cointegration information. These substantially expand the formal justification.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about connecting non-stationarity with dependency modeling, TimeBridge's two attention mechanisms, and forecasting performance. Added supporting analysis does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds a dataset-specific explanation that hybrid MAE particularly helps fluctuating, low-channel ETT data, while loss choice matters less on higher-channel datasets. v3 offered only a general training-stability rationale. The main high-dimensional forecasting discussion also shifts from Climate to Traffic.

D1.justification: v4 newly states that test batches are not dropped, removes the batch-size disclosure of 16 for Electricity/Traffic and 32 elsewhere, and revises Table 8's settings. Table 7 corrects ETTh sampling intervals to one hour, matching the existing prose. Hardware, software, and code-access disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including Leddam, DUET, TFB, TimeFilter, and other recent work, while removing the Monash archive citation associated with Climate. The normalization/dependency taxonomy and central novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v4 inserts a theoretical appendix and loss discussion, renumbers subsequent appendices, and adds acknowledgements and conference/author-note updates. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the loss-comparison Table 15, reduces the financial uncertainty table's columns, changes comparator columns, and removes Climate rows. Appendix tables are regrouped and Figure 6 is relocated relative to surrounding tables. The fourteen existing figures are retained without substantive visual changes.

improvement.justification: The new loss control helps assess whether performance depends on the training objective, and the updated baselines improve comparison coverage. However, v4 removes the highest-dimensional Climate evaluation and uncertainty estimates for three financial metrics. Its new theoretical justification also contains an internal inconsistency: Proposition 1 claims quadratic growth in time although its displayed formula is linear in time. These competing gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
